name: Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd
title: Gaja Alternative Asset Management Ltd - 544885 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Asset manager with ~INR1,106 crore net worth post-IPO; H1 PAT up 48% to INR91.9 crore, but LTM fee income (INR61.3 crore) roughly equals opex (INR63.4 crore) and carry is realised-only from Fund II.

triggers.label: Fund V target INR2,500 crore; secondaries INR1,500 crore
triggers.quote: We have received SEBI approval for seeking commitments of INR2,500 crores.

guidance.quote: We have received SEBI approval for seeking commitments of INR2,500 crores.

red_flags.label: Fee income roughly equals opex; profit reliant on realised carry and one-off tax write-back
red_flags.quote: This quarter's profit includes a write -back of INR15 crore s from a lower provision for tax

red_flags.label: Carry only on realised basis; Fund II carry drives recent growth
red_flags.quote: We only book carry on realized basis.

evasions.topic: Fund III hurdle status / carry timing
evasions.quote: So, the IRR of the fund does not matter. What matters is where is the fund in terms of liquidating that particular multiple on invested capital.

summary.headline: Gaja AMC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 138% QoQ to INR64.7 crore, helped by a INR15 crore deferred tax write-back; H1 PAT up 48% to INR91.9 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR65.5 crore, up 26% QoQ, and PAT was INR64.7 crore, up 138% QoQ and 54% YoY, though the quarter includes a INR15 crore deferred tax reversal. H1 total income grew 6% to INR117.3 crore while H1 performance income fell to INR75.9 crore from INR78.5 crore, reflecting realisation timing. Net worth rose 92% YoY to INR1,106 crore after the IPO, with the company nearly debt-free and INR690 crore in cash and liquid investments. Management framed the balance sheet as capacity for roughly INR8,000 crore of new sponsor commitments, with Fund V and Eastgate Secondaries still raising.

financial_highlights.change: up 138% QoQ, up 54% YoY; includes INR15 crore deferred tax write-back
up 55% QoQ, driven by Fund II carry
vs INR78.5 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Management fee
segments.commentary: Fee income was flat at about INR15 crore in Q2; LTM fee income INR61.3 crore (37% of LTM total income) against LTM total expenses of INR63.4 crore.

segments.name: Performance income (carry and sponsor gains)
segments.commentary: Q2 performance income INR46.2 crore, mainly carry from Fund II's significant exit; LTM performance income INR85.4 crore (52% of total income). Carry is booked only on realised basis, European waterfall with full catch-up.

segments.name: Treasury income
segments.commentary: LTM treasury income INR18.1 crore (11% of total income); management now calls it a fourth pillar after the IPO-funded balance sheet.

segments.name: Fund portfolio
segments.commentary: Fund IV (INR1,775 crore, final close 2023): 9 investments, 87% deployed, 2.0x gross multiple. Fund III: 10 investments, partially realised, 1.9x. Fund II: substantially realised, 3.8x. Fund I: fully realised, 5.6x.

guidance_outlook: Fund V seeks INR2,500 crore (SEBI approved), 10-year term extendable by two years; management says it takes about 18 months from launch to final close, with management fee earned from first close.
Eastgate Secondaries Fund I seeks INR1,500 crore, 5-year term extendable by two years, targeting List A GP portfolios.
Management expects a transition period as Fund II ends, with carry from subsequent funds arriving over coming years.
Sponsor commitment target raised to 10% of fund size over time; current capacity estimated at about INR8,000 crore of new funds at 8.4%.
Interim dividend of INR0.50 per share declared (10% of face value), after a INR0.75 final dividend for FY26.
capex_capacity: IPO fresh issue of INR450 crore: INR372 crore earmarked for sponsor commitments to Fund IV, Fund V and Eastgate, and INR78 crore for general corporate purposes.
As of 30 Sep 2026, about 10% of the sponsor commitment allocation and about 80% of the general corporate purposes allocation has been utilised.
Sponsor commitments total INR589 crore (7.1% of fund size), including Fund II 6%, Fund III 4.4%, Fund IV 8.5%, proposed Fund V 8.4%, proposed Eastgate 7%.
Balance sheet: total assets INR1,176.5 crore; non-current investments INR459.6 crore; cash and bank INR450 crore; current investments INR165.4 crore.
demand_pricing: AIF commitments in India INR16.9 trillion in FY26, 29% CAGR since FY19; CRISIL projects 25-27% growth to FY30 (INR41-44 trillion).
NPS permitted to invest in Cat I and II AIFs since January 2026 and began active commitments in October 2026; insurers and banks are opening up but nascent.
Investor network: 298 LPs in existing funds and about 900 investors across more than 20 countries; most capital raised directly, with fewer distributors than typical.
Target market: mid-market companies with enterprise value up to INR2,000 crore, scaling to INR10,000 crore; about 2,300 companies mapped in the four sector themes, growing about 25% a year.
Analyst challenge on fee income not covering opex: management says fee plus treasury income covers total expenses; carry is realised-only and Fund III is not yet explicitly stated as above hurdle.

qa_highlights.question: Fee income (INR61 crore LTM) does not cover opex (INR63 crore), so is profit all from carry? Is Fund III above hurdle, and what gross multiple is needed before the first carry rupee?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said carry is booked only on a realised basis, so IRR does not matter; the fund must return principal and hurdle first. LTM fee INR61.3 crore vs expenses INR63.4 crore; fee plus treasury income covers expenses. Carry currently comes from Fund II, with sponsor gains from Fund III and IV.

qa_highlights.question: Where are the most interesting investing opportunities in India and what is the worldview?
qa_highlights.answer: Four sectors (intelligent software and automation, deep tech and AI, financial services, consumer, EEE) with about 2,300 mapped companies growing about 25% a year; newer sectors growing about twice as fast. Management said it is a long-term bull on India, with nominal growth of 11-12%.

risks_watch: Earnings quality: Q2 PAT includes a INR15 crore deferred tax reversal tied to revised sponsor-gain tax estimates on new auditors' advice; underlying PBT growth was 13% QoQ-type metrics, 20% for H1.
Carry dependence: LTM performance income is 52% of total income, and carry currently rests on Fund II; the timing of future realisations (Fund III, IV) drives lumpy income.
Fundraising execution: Fund V (INR2,500 crore) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crore) are still raising; the 18-month close timeline and fee catch-up mechanics affect near-term fee income.
Fee coverage: management fee alone (INR61.3 crore) is roughly equal to LTM opex (INR63.4 crore).
ROE dilution: 13% ROE reflects IPO cash held in treasury until deployed into sponsor commitments; watch deployment pace versus the 10% of allocation used so far.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the balance sheet, fundraising capacity and fund performance, with a clear tone on the four-pillar model. Evasive on carry timing: management declined to say whether Fund III is above hurdle, and answered by restating the realised-only carry policy.
key_quotes: Our strong balance sheet now earns treasury income, a fourth pillar of growth alongside management fees, carried interest, and gains on sponsor commitments.
We only book carry on realized basis. So, the IRR of the fund does not matter.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; growth depends on Fund V (INR2,500 crore target, SEBI approved) and Eastgate Secondaries (INR1,500 crore), with about INR8,000 crore of sponsor capacity, but fundraising is still in progress and carry is realised-only, so outlook is flat-to-uncertain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost-to-income fell to 29% in H1 FY27 from 38% a year ago and total expenses dropped 17% to INR34.6 crore, but performance income (carry) is lumpy and H1 performance income fell to INR75.9 crore from INR78.5 crore, so margins depend on realisation timing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity is the balance sheet: about INR8,000 crore of new sponsor commitment capacity at 8.4%, with INR690 crore in cash and liquid investments and only about 10% of the INR372 crore sponsor allocation used so far, but the Fund V and Eastgate raises are still in progress, so this is fund capacity rather than physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 total income grew 6% YoY to INR117.3 crore, and fee income was flat at about INR15 crore in Q2, so AUM growth depends on Fund V (INR2,500 crore target) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crore) closing, which management says takes about 18 months from launch.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Sponsor commitments total INR589 crore (7.1% of fund size), and utilisation of the IPO sponsor allocation is only about 10%, so a new sponsor commitment is more likely to come as Fund V and Eastgate close than as a physical capex announcement; no new plant or facility was discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was given, and performance income fell in H1 to INR75.9 crore from INR78.5 crore, with carry realised only and Fund III's hurdle status not confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management fee of INR61.3 crore LTM roughly equals LTM opex of INR63.4 crore, and Q2 PAT of INR64.7 crore was helped by a INR15 crore deferred tax write-back that will not recur, so underlying earnings could look weaker if carry realisations slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fund V (INR2,500 crore, SEBI approved) and Eastgate Secondaries Fund I (INR1,500 crore) are both raising now, and the treasury 'fourth pillar' is a new revenue stream after the IPO.

rows.label: Fund V and Eastgate first closes add fee base
rows.why: Management fee is earned from first close, and Fund V targets INR2,500 crore plus Eastgate INR1,500 crore, against LTM fee income of INR61.3 crore, though the close takes about 18 months from launch.

rows.label: Net cash balance sheet deployment
rows.why: Borrowings fell to INR0.2 crore from INR33.5 crore and cash plus liquid investments are INR690 crore, while ROE fell to 13% from 19% because IPO cash sits idle until deployed into sponsor commitments.

rows.label: Carry realisation from Fund II and Fund III
rows.why: Q2 performance income rose 55% QoQ to INR46.2 crore mainly from Fund II's significant exit, but Fund II is substantially realised and Fund III (1.9x, partially realised) carry timing is unclear.

tone.note: Management was confident on the balance sheet, fundraising capacity and fund performance, but evasive on Fund III's hurdle status and carry timing; analysts pressed on fee income not covering opex and on the INR15 crore deferred tax write-back inflating PAT.
